title: Subscriber prefill demultiplexer with quarantine rollback plan
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: implement a low-latency speculative prefill demultiplexer ("subscriber-prefill") that probes multiple candidate model runtimes/kernels in parallel, computes an acceptance signal using a compact confidence drift metric, and safely quarantines/rolls back to a conservative path when signals are weak. This work sits at the intersection of kernel selection, attention path pruning, and prefill/decode scheduling.

Background: current speculative routing probes a single fast path and falls back to a slower but more reliable path when acceptance metrics fail. For some workloads we can reduce wasted work by running lightweight subscriber-prefill probes across a small set of candidate kernels (e.g., quantized vs fp16 kernels, attention-optimized vs generic), then demultiplexing to the best candidate for the remainder of the request. The complexity arises from measurement noise (logit drift early in decode), kernel warmup costs, and capacity accounting.

Design proposal summary:
- Probe model: issue a short prefill (N tokens or until a sentinel) to up to 2 candidate runtimes in parallel: a "fast" candidate (aggressive quantized kernel + attention pruning) and a "stable" candidate (safer kernel, full attention). Probes must be limited to minimal KV allocations and use a shared allocator to avoid double memory blowups.
- Acceptance metric: compute a compact confidence-drift score combining (1) max-logit margin, (2) normalized softmax entropy delta, and (3) embedding cosine similarity against the stable-path embedding. These are combined with a small learned linear weight vector derived from offline evals to give a single acceptance score. Thresholds are percentile-based per-model and per-sequence-length.
- Demux decision: if fast candidate score >= threshold + hysteresis => commit to fast path; if stable candidate is higher => commit to stable; if ambiguous (within hysteresis band) => continue speculative streaming while concurrently preparing the fallback path and mark request for soft-eviction policy.
- Quarantine & rollback: if downstream quality regressions are detected (post-commit), the commit decision triggers a rolling quarantine period for the fast candidate on that model-version/pool. Quarantine includes reducing traffic weight and increasing accept threshold for subsequent requests for a decay window (e.g., 30 minutes with exponential backoff).
- Safety: ensure that probes do not increase p95 latency beyond the SLO by bounding probe runtime to a fixed microsecond budget and enabling circuit-breaker on slow probes. Prefill probe counts and sizes configurable per-customer.

Engineering tasks:
- Runtime: add subscriber-prefill path in the scheduler, with KV cache lightweight clones and cross-kernel shared allocator hooks.
- Kernel selection: extend kernel catalog metadata to expose warmup cost, steady-state throughput, and attention-optimized capability flags.
- Acceptance scoring: implement compact on-host scorer with percentile-configured thresholds and offline calibration tooling.
- Observability: new telemetry for probe latency, acceptance_score distribution, commit rates, revert/quarantine events, and per-candidate wasted compute.
- Rollout: feature-flagged canary with traffic weights and automatic rollback on SLA regressions.

Perf targets: reduce end-to-end p50 for qualifying workloads by 10-20% vs current stable path while keeping p95 within 5% of baseline. Keep additional cost per-request due to probes under 12% in steady state.

Risks & mitigations:
- Memory blowup from parallel prefill: mitigate via shared allocator + configurable small probe size.
- False acceptance causing quality regressions: use conservative hysteresis and short probation windows before wide traffic shifts.
- Telemetry noise: collect per-token and per-prefill metrics and run offline A/B on labeled prompt sets before promoting thresholds.

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end implementation behind a runtime feature flag.
- Canary on 5% of traffic for two weeks with no customer-facing regressions and telemetry showing expected commit/discard rates.
- Observability dashboards and runbooks created and linked in comments.
